title: Disposition beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts under the permanent-evidence policy
description:
Same defect class as eshyra-4tgd, which was deliberately scoped to
packages/core/test/reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts only.

packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts has the same shape:
AGENTS.md prose -> regex asserting AGENTS.md still contains equivalent prose.
Its five tests read AGENTS.md and pin the PR-deliverable bead-lifecycle wording,
the "Judge by **deliverable**, not by agent role." sentence, the note that the
rule narrows the generated bd close checklist, and a section-order relation.

Apply the same disposition analysis eshyra-4tgd used; see that bead's ledger for
the format and for the blanket replacement responsibility. Do NOT assume the
outcome transfers: at least two assertions there may be genuinely structural
rather than semantic mirrors —

- the section-order check (Session Completion ahead of PR Merge Policy), which
  may or may not encode a semantic dependency the way the disposition gate does;
- 'does not strand the rule in the supervisor-only hook', which reads
  .claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs and asserts a rule is NOT confined to a
  surface only one agent can read. That observes a real cross-surface topology
  between an executable hook and common authority, and is the strongest
  candidate for retention in that file.

Verify each independently against the documents and the hook as they exist then.

EXCLUSIONS: same as eshyra-4tgd. No replacement schema, snapshot, hash, manifest,
baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker; do not relocate the
same mirrors into another file; do not replace many regexes with one large one.
notes:
DISPOSITION LEDGER (2026-09-22), same format as eshyra-4tgd: existing evidence -> claimed invariant -> authority -> actual boundary -> disposition -> replacement.

OUTCOME: all 5 tests RETIRED, file deleted (94 lines, 5 tests, 8 expect() -> 0). The bead warned the eshyra-4tgd outcome may not transfer and named two assertions as possible genuine structure; both were checked independently against the documents and the hook as they exist now, and neither held.

BLANKET REPLACEMENT RESPONSIBILITY for every retired assertion: what AGENTS.md MEANS is owned by the authority hierarchy (AGENTS.md itself), the owning Bead or accepted design, and semantic-system review of any change to that authority. A regex copy of editable authority cannot establish that a FUTURE version of it is valid - an authorized bad edit updates document and regex together, while a legitimate rewording breaks the regex. Demonstrated empirically below, in both directions.

ORIGINAL AUTHORITY, checked: eshyra-o9bd.19.16 (PR #519, merge f0fad2a, sole commit touching this file: 5866b305). Its SCOPE authorized three deliverables - state the rule in AGENTS.md Session Completion scoped by deliverable; state that it narrows the generated bd-prime checklist; replace the hook's inline sentence with a pointer. None authorizes permanent executable ownership of the rule's WORDING. Its close reason says 'packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts pins it', which makes the file a DELIVERY artifact of that bead, not a durable invariant - the identical finding eshyra-4tgd reached about its own old test 2.

RETIRED, tests 1-3 (prose mirrors, uncontested): 'states that a PR-deliverable bead stays in_progress until merge'; 'scopes the rule by deliverable so dispatched children still close'; 'records that it narrows the generated bd close checklist'. Each is AGENTS.md prose -> regex asserting AGENTS.md still contains equivalent prose.

RETIRED, test 4 'keeps the rule in Session Completion, ahead of PR Merge Policy' - the section-order relation the bead flagged. It does NOT encode a semantic dependency the way eshyra-4tgd's disposition-gate ordering claimed to. Three independent failures: (a) it locates the RULE by a prose substring, so a one-word synonym swap breaks it; (b) it identifies both sections by heading TEXT, the exact proxy class eshyra-4tgd retired at bc277005; (c) raw indexOf with no existence check - renaming '### Session Completion' yields -1 and 'rule > -1' passes, so the rule may be moved ANYWHERE. Verified: heading renamed and the whole rule relocated to the top of AGENTS.md, guard green. No authority requires that placement, and a section move inside one document is fully visible in its diff.

RETIRED, test 5 'does not strand the rule in the supervisor-only hook' - the bead's strongest retention candidate. The claim is real (a general lifecycle rule must not live only on a Claude-injected surface Codex can never execute) but the implementation observes none of it, and is vacuous in BOTH halves. (a) expect(hook).toContain('AGENTS.md') is satisfied by the hook's own header comment, which says to keep supervisor policy OUT of AGENTS.md - plus three further incidental mentions. It passes with the pointer deleted. (b) The negative regex pins ONE historical sentence ('handoff stops at an open PR...'), so restating the stranded rule in any other words passes. Verified: the AGENTS.md pointer removed from the Bead-per-dispatch bullet and the rule re-stranded as 'Keep the parent bead open until its pull request lands on main; do not close it at PR-open' - guard green, i.e. the precise defect eshyra-o9bd.19.16 existed to close reproduces undetected. Deeper reason it cannot be repaired rather than retired: the harmful state is 'rule present ONLY in the hook', whose detection requires knowing the rule is present in AGENTS.md - which is a prose mirror again. The cross-surface topology is not machine-identifiable without text identity, so it belongs to semantic-system review of changes to AGENTS.md and the hook.

ADVERSARIAL EVIDENCE (empirical, all mutations applied to the tree and verified by inspection, then reverted):
BAD states that PASS, with no test edited: (1) rule gutted by appending 'An agent may instead close the bead at PR-open whenever it judges the work finished.' - 5/5 pass; (2) '### Session Completion' renamed to '### Wrapping Up a Session' and the entire rule block relocated under the H1 - 5/5 pass; (3) hook pointer replaced by a reworded restatement of the rule - 5/5 pass; (4) hook file deleted outright - 5/5 pass (by design, existsSync early return).
GOOD states that FAIL: 'pull request stays in_progress' -> 'remains in_progress' - 2 failed / 3 passed, including the supposedly structural ordering test; 'Judge by **deliverable**, not by agent role.' -> 'Judge by the **deliverable**, not by the agent's role.' - 1 failed / 4 passed.

NOT USED as justification: runtime cost. The file ran in ~95ms; it was never the problem and is not the reason.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: a reachability guard on .claude/settings.json -> supervisor-context.mjs -> codex-subagent-workflow.md, the one candidate in this area whose identity is not document text (sibling of the retained commonAuthorityStructure link guard). Declined: it is a DIFFERENT responsibility from anything this file ever claimed, the hook is optional Claude Code tooling whose absence is loud rather than silent (the seat charter already directs a session without it to operate under ordinary AGENTS.md authority), and inventing it here would be new proof machinery outside this bead's scope and against its exclusions.

EXCLUSIONS HONORED: no replacement schema, snapshot, hash, manifest, baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker; no mirror relocated to another file; no many-regexes-into-one consolidation; no test added to prove the removal safe. No tombstone memory, registry, or appendix. Nothing referenced this file anywhere in the tree (verified by repo-wide grep) and no bd memory names it.

DOCUMENTS UNCHANGED: the lifecycle rule in AGENTS.md and the hook's pointer are untouched by this PR. Provenance stays in eshyra-o9bd.19.16, PR #519, the hook's own citation of that bead, and Git/Dolt history.

MEASUREMENTS: 94 -> 0 lines, 5 -> 0 tests, 8 -> 0 expect(). verify:worktree clean - 5,608 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed, 5 fewer tests than main; format/check/typecheck all exit 0. measure-run: 46.5s wall, peak process-tree RSS 2877 MB.

PRE-EXISTING, not ridden along: biome.json pins schema 2.5.12 against installed Biome 2.5.13, one info-level diagnostic present on main. Filed as eshyra-3wsg per the dependency-PR separation rule.

PR #561 opened (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/561), head 4ace7533, branch eshyra-5wbx, base main at 29f6c2f9. Stays in_progress until that PR merges, per AGENTS.md Session Completion.
PR #561 MERGED 2026-09-22 (merge commit e7bb1836, reviewed head 4ace7533). Deliverable landed on main; bead closed. Worktree and branch removed. Follow-up filed: eshyra-3wsg (biome.json schema re-migration, pre-existing, deliberately not ridden along).
close_reason: Merged to main as PR #561, merge commit e7bb1836. All five prose-mirror assertions in packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts retired and the file deleted, with adversarial evidence in both directions recorded in the disposition ledger above.
